story.title: Shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square Leaves Six Dead and Over a Dozen Injured
story.summary: A shooting incident in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland, resulted in six fatalities and at least 15 injuries. The gunman, a Polish citizen, reportedly opened fire from his car before being shot and wounded by police. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding this tragic event, which is notable as mass shootings are rare in Poland.

explore_lenses.label: Why is this attack especially consequential?
explore_lenses.title: A rare mass-casualty attack in a civic center
explore_lenses.summary: The shooting struck Kraków’s central public square and produced an unusually high casualty toll for Poland. It is likely to prompt scrutiny of public-space security and firearms access, but officials have not established whether the weapons used were legally held.

claims.text: The attack occurred around 3 p.m. in the area of Sławkowska Street on the Main Market Square, and the city activated a crisis staff while emergency services worked at the scene.
Associated Press reported that mass shootings are uncommon in Poland; that makes an attack that killed six people and injured 15 a major break from the country’s usual pattern of gun violence.

Polish law generally requires a police-issued firearms permit outside specified exceptions, but it remains unknown whether the firearm used in Kraków or weapons recovered from the suspect’s car were legal.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about the attack’s path?
explore_lenses.title: The shooting extended beyond the square
explore_lenses.summary: Official and local accounts indicate a mobile attack, rather than a single stationary incident: the assailant fired from a car in the square and was later stopped elsewhere in central Kraków. That wider path is relevant to investigators reconstructing timing, targets, and police use of force.

claims.text: Kraków’s city government said the assailant allegedly fired from a passing car in the Main Market Square area and was shot and detained by police near the Dietla–Stradomska intersection.

The municipal transit operator reported that a person firing from a passenger car also shot at a No. 1 tram at Plac Wszystkich Świętych, breaking the driver’s-cab window; it said neither the driver nor passengers were injured.
Police said the attacker was a Polish national and that no second perpetrator was at large; reporting also said two police officers were among those injured during the arrest.
Officials have not announced a motive, identified any intended targets, or released a complete account of the pursuit and exchange of gunfire.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the investigation?
explore_lenses.title: Evidence collection and victim care come first
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate official response is an active criminal investigation alongside medical treatment and scene management. Because the suspect was wounded and hospitalized, the timing and nature of any formal charges are not yet known.

claims.text: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said police were investigating the background and all circumstances of the attack; Kraków’s mayor said the city crisis staff was operating.
The Guardian reported that prosecutors, police and other services were at the scene securing evidence and investigating the circumstances.
The regional governor said 12 of the injured were in life-threatening condition, meaning the confirmed death toll and injury assessments could still change.
The suspect was reported hospitalized after being shot by police, so any charging decision depends on his medical condition and the evidence gathered by prosecutors.

story_report.summary: Six people were killed and at least 15 wounded after a Polish citizen allegedly opened fire from a car in Kraków’s Main Market Square area on Nov. 7. The attack occurred around 3 p.m. near Sławkowska Street, prompting the city to activate its crisis staff as emergency services responded. Police shot and detained the suspect near the Dietla–Stradomska intersection; he was later reported hospitalized. The scale of the attack was unusual in Poland, where mass shootings are uncommon.

sections.heading: Attack and police response
sections.body: Kraków’s municipal transit operator said a person firing from a passenger car also shot at a No. 1 tram at Plac Wszystkich Świętych, shattering the driver’s-cab window. The operator said the driver and passengers were not injured. Police said no second perpetrator was at large, while reporting indicated that two officers were among those injured during the arrest. The regional governor said 12 injured people were in life-threatening condition.

sections.heading: Gun laws and investigation
sections.body: Polish law generally requires a police-issued firearms permit outside specified exceptions. The reported attack therefore stands apart from the country’s usual pattern of gun violence, according to Associated Press reporting that mass shootings are uncommon in Poland. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said police were examining the background and circumstances of the attack, while prosecutors, police and other services secured evidence at the scene.

unresolved.text: Officials had not announced a motive, identified intended targets, or provided a complete account of the pursuit and exchange of gunfire.
Authorities had not publicly said what weapons were used, how they were obtained, or whether the firearm and any weapons recovered from the suspect’s car were legal.
No charging timetable, forensic findings or final casualty accounting had been announced; the suspect’s medical condition may affect charging decisions.

related_stories.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Sentenced to 200 Years for Murdering 191 People
related_stories.summary: Paul Mackenzie, the leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect, has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult. The court found that he incited his followers to starve themselves and their families in a bid to 'meet Jesus.' Mackenzie and 28 accomplices were convicted for their roles in this tragic incident.

related_stories.title: Thomas Markle Arrested on Child Sexual Abuse Material Charges
related_stories.summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, has been arrested in Florida on charges of possessing child sexual abuse materials. The Justice Department reported that the allegations include having sexually explicit photographs involving minors. Following his arrest, Markle appeared in court and is currently under house arrest after the FBI conducted searches of storage units he rented in the Los Angeles area.

related_stories.title: Jay Rockefeller, Former Governor and Senator, Passes Away at 89
related_stories.summary: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family's political dynasty, has died at the age of 89. He served as the governor of West Virginia and was a longtime U.S. senator, known for his advocacy on healthcare, education, and working families' needs. Rockefeller was born into a prominent family and forged a significant political career.
